standard.title: General Conditions for Delivery and Inspection of Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products
standard.sector: Metallurgical Engineering / Light Metals and their Alloys

sectional_committee.name: Light Metals and Their Alloys Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the general requirements, administrative guidelines, sampling scales, mechanical/chemical testing regimes, defect criteria, tolerances, and packaging protocols that govern the supply, delivery, and quality inspection of all wrought and cast aluminium and aluminium alloy products (such as sheets, plates, coils, strips, bars, rods, profiles, tubes, wires, forgings, and castings). It serves as the master technical delivery and compliance framework wrapped around individual product specifications.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the general requirements, administrative guidelines, sampling scales, mechanical/chemical testing regimes, defect criteria, tolerances, and packaging protocols that govern the supply, delivery, and quality inspection of all wrought and cast aluminium and aluminium alloy products (such as sheets, plates, coils, strips, bars, rods, profiles, tubes, wires, forgings, and castings). It serves as the master technical delivery and compliance framework wrapped around individual product specifications.

certification.description: Master Administrative Reference Framework. IS 10259 is not a primary product certification standard (not directly certified under a separate voluntary or mandatory license) but rather serves as the mandatory technical delivery, sampling, and inspection code referenced by downstream product standards. Any manufacturer producing aluminium corrugated sheets, wrought plates, or castings under mandatory or voluntary BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) schemes (such as IS 1254, IS 737, or IS 617) must perform routine quality control, sampling, batch selection, defect reviews, retesting, and rust-proof packaging in strict accordance with IS 10259. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.
requirements: General requirements relating to the supply, inspection, and verification of chemical/mechanical parameters of aluminium products must conform to the master framework of IS 10259.

Products must be smooth, clean, and completely free from harmful surface defects such as cracks, severe draw lines, lamination slivers, edge splitting, pitting, corrosion scale, or foreign inclusions that would compromise structural ductility or load capacity.

If any primary test specimen fails to meet chemical or mechanical properties during quality auditing, a strict retest protocol applies: a) Two additional test samples must be selected at random from the same lot; b) If both retests conform, the entire lot is deemed to have passed; c) If either retest specimen fails, the entire lot represented shall be rejected.

Materials of the same alloy designation, size, nominal thickness, and temper condition must be grouped together into a single control unit or lot (defined as up to 300 tubes, 1000 kg, or as specified by product codes) for statistical testing, ensuring traceable representation.

Samples must be prepared and analyzed per IS 504 parts or equivalent instrumental techniques (such as Spark Optical Emission Spectroscopy) to verify that heavy metals and alloy concentrations stay within specification boundaries.

Packaging methods must ensure full protection of the polished or rolled aluminium surfaces. The packing mode must prevent mechanical bending or denting and completely isolate the metals from moisture ingress to eliminate transit water staining or white rust corrosion.

All mechanical checks must be evaluated in the exact delivery temper or condition requested by the purchaser (such as O - Annealed, H14 - Half-hard, or T6 - Solution Treated and Artificially Aged) per IS 5052 temper designations.
